name: Howard Heller
life: “I still remember a keyring from the place where I got my first job.” People around Breakwater Way know Howard by a small Thursday habit. Howard stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I came prepared to laugh at the performance. My car keys became the last instrument in it.
appearance: Howard has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Howard rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Howard can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To bring the car keys back for the next concert.
family: Faye Tate is Howard’s cousin raised in the same household. Howard brings a spare shopping bag. Faye chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The crash anniversary*, Faye says, “I take flowers home after they wilt so the family doesn't have to see them wet and gray.”
connections: Malcolm Tan. Keys and the old packing tin place a shop closing inside the music.

reactions.situation: An instrument breaks before the fountain piece begins
reactions.response: Howard asks the player whether a different everyday object can carry the missing note.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Howard asks each person to say what they believe is actually owed before anybody proposes a payment.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Howard asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
